design_gotchas.title: Internal Back-to-Back Differential Input Clamp Diodes Limit Comparator Use
design_gotchas.detail: Per Maximum Ratings Note 1 and Figure 1, each amplifier includes parallel back-to-back diodes across the inverting and noninverting inputs. Applying large differential voltages without series current-limiting resistors conducts excessive input current; do not use directly as an open-loop comparator.

design_gotchas.title: Bipolar NPN/PNP Input Stage Flips Bias Current Polarity Near VEE + 0.8 V
design_gotchas.detail: The all-bipolar rail-to-rail input stage switches from PNP to NPN around VEE + 0.8 V (page 9, Figure 6), reversing the 80 nA typ (200 nA max) input bias current and creating offset step errors with high-impedance sources compared to 5 pA CMOS op-amps like TLV9002IDR.

design_gotchas.title: 80 mA High Output Current vs 658 mW SOIC-8 Thermal Derating Limit
design_gotchas.detail: Current-boosted outputs drive 600 Ω loads and deliver 80 mA typ short-circuit current, so sustained heavy loads at 12 V supply can rapidly exceed the ~658 mW SOIC-8 power dissipation limit at 25°C (RθJA ≈ 190 °C/W, TJ,max = 150°C).

design_gotchas.title: 12 V Operating / 13 V Absolute Max Ceiling vs 30 V–36 V Industrial Op-Amps
design_gotchas.detail: MC33202DR2G spans 1.8 V to 12 V (wider than 5.5 V LMV358IDR/TLV9002IDR), but its 13 V absolute maximum rating prevents drop-in replacement on ±15 V (30 V) or 24 V LM358DR/TL072IDR/OPA2134UA rails.

engineering_summary: The onsemi MC33202DR2G is a dual all-bipolar rail-to-rail input and output (RRIO) operational amplifier in an 8-pin SOIC (CASE 751) package spanning 1.8 V to 12 V (13 V abs max) over -40°C to +105°C. Sharing the standard dual SOIC-8 pinout with LM358DR, LMV358IDR, and TLV9002IDR, it stands out for its current-boosted 600 Ω / 80 mA output drive, 2.2 MHz GBWP, 20 nV/√Hz noise, and phase-reversal immunity up to 200 mV beyond rails. Key tradeoffs include 80 nA bipolar input bias current with polarity reversal near VEE + 0.8 V, 0.9 mA/ch quiescent current, and internal back-to-back input clamp diodes.
